newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Dell busy ahead of earnings.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Dell busy ahead of earnings.

text.p: Options on Dell Computer Corp were active Tuesday ahead of the computer maker's fiscal second quarter earnings, scheduled for release after the close of trading, traders said.
Dell shares were up 2-1/4 at 84-1/2 on more than 9.5 million shares in afternoon activity.
"Everybody's waiting. Everybody's got their positions," an options trader said.
He said his desk had not done much Dell trading today but most investors had been buying calls earlier, with some investors buying puts to protect underlying stock positions.
The Dell September 85 call was the most active Dell option, with 6,930 contracts changing hands. The September 90 call traded 4,025 and the September 95 call traded 3,755.
Among the puts, the September 80 traded 3,465, the September 70 traded about 3,300 and the September 75 traded 1,825.
One options trader in Chicago said his desk had traded some Dell puts and calls and that there was not a clear directional bias in the activity.
Dell is expected to post $0.54 per share for its fiscal second quarter, according to first call.
The company earned $0.29 a share in the second quarter last year.

"Tomorrow should be interesting," the options trader said, referring to a reaction in Dell shares. He noted that over the last few quarters, Dell shares have dropped after the company's quarterly earnings even though they beat estimates.
"Every time they came out and said 'we had good numbers but our next quarter is going to be soft,'" he said.
Robert Walberg, chief equity analyst at Briefing.com, said what Dell says about its future earnings will be more important than the numbers it posts.
But he added that since the company has been able to beat estimates by around 25 percent recently, if they only top current estimates by 10 percent, for example, some investors may be disappointed.
"The bar is set pretty high," he said.
Implied volatilities in Dell options were mostly in the mid-60 region, up from a historical average of 43 in July.
Traders said they expected volatility to decline sharply Wednesday, after the earnings news is out.
In other activity, Gateway 2000 Inc options were busy as the stock rallied sharply.

Traders said Gateway, which was up 3-5/16 at 40-9/16 in heavy trading, was boosted by news that one of its main shippers, the United Parcel Service, had reached a tentative agreement with striking Teamsters workers that would end a 15-day strike.
A Gateway options market maker in Chicago said many investors had positioned themselves for an upturn in the stock and were now cashing out by liquidating call positions.
The September 32-1/2 calls, the September 40 calls and the September 32-1/2 puts were among the busiest Gateway options.
